primary_outcome_instrument_scale: Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), 11-point scale 0 ('no pain') to 10 ('worst imaginable pain')
primary_timepoint: 2 weeks post-intervention ('2nd week measurement'), after 4 manual-therapy sessions over two weeks
arms: Group 1: Mulligan mobilisation + home-based Therapeutic Exercise (TE) (n=14)
contrast_reported_primary: Three pairwise between-group comparisons reported at each timepoint in Table 2: a = Group 1 (Mulligan+TE) vs Group 2 (Maitland+TE); b = Group 1 vs Group 3 (TE-alone control); c = Group 2 vs Group 3. The paper's actual primary inferential test is the omnibus 3-group x time interaction from the Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA (for NPRS: F=0.983, p=0.383, not significant); pairwise Tukey HSD comparisons are described as post hoc, triggered only when this interaction is significant. Our registry's declared contrast 'Arm 1 vs Arm 2' corresponds to the paper's 'a' contrast, i.e. Group 1 (Mulligan+TE) vs Group 2 (Maitland+TE) -- a head-to-head comparison of the two active manual-therapy arms, not a comparison against the true (TE-alone) control group.
population_detail: Adults of both genders, aged 18-40 years (mean age 31.91 +/- 2.33 years), with acute, subacute, or chronic Non-Specific Neck Pain (NSNP), inclusion required NPRS > 2. Excluded: pregnancy, systemic diseases, recent whiplash (<=6 months), prior cervical/thoracic surgery, upper cervical pathology, osteoporosis, severe medical conditions, neurological symptoms, positive red-flag tests. Recruited and treated at the Department of Physiotherapy, International Hellenic University (IHU), Thessaloniki, Greece, February-March 2025.

published_estimate.quote: 'A Two-Way Repeated Measures Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was conducted to examine between-group differences (Mulligan + Home Exercise versus Maitland + Home Exercise versus Home Exercise only) and within-group changes over time. When a significant group x time interaction was found, post hoc pairwise comparisons between groups at each time point were performed using Tukey's HSD test.' (Statistical analysis, p.72). Results, NPRS subsection (p.72-73): 'Pain intensity significantly decreased in all groups. The Mulligan group showed a mean NPRS reduction of 2.43 points (4.79+/-1.63 to 2.36+/-1.45), the Maitland group had a 2.93-point reduction (5.07+/-1.54 to 2.14+/-1.51), and the control group exhibited a 2.27-point reduction (5.07+/-1.87 to 2.80+/-1.32) (Table 2). ... the group x time interaction was not statistically significant (F=0.983, p=0.383), suggesting that all interventions were equally effective, with no technique proving superior.' Table 2 (p.73), NPRS row, between-group p-values: baseline p^a(1v2)=0.896, p^b(1v3)=0.896, p^c(2v3)=1.000; 2nd week p^a(1v2)=0.917, p^b(1v3)=0.683, p^c(2v3)=0.437; Interaction p=0.383/F=0.983.

B_covariate_list: None entered in the primary outcome model. Age and Sex (registry: 'Age,Gender') were tested only for between-group baseline balance (Table 1: one-way ANOVA / Pearson chi-square, all p>0.05) and were not used as covariates in the Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA for NPRS or any other outcome; no ANCOVA-adjusted primary model is reported.
data_availability_statement: The data supporting the findings of this study are openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15278572, reference number 15278572.
journal: Hong Kong Physiotherapy Journal (Vol. 46, No. 1 (2026), 67-82; DOI: 10.1142/S1013702526500058)

registry_check.issues: (1) ARM/CONTROL MISMATCH: the SPSS file's TreatmentGroup variable has embedded value labels 1='Mulligan', 2='Maitland', 3='Control' (confirmed by reading the .sav metadata directly with pyreadstat). The paper's actual control/comparator group is the home-exercise-only arm ('Home Exercise only' / Group 3 / 'TE group'), which is coded TreatmentGroup=3, NOT TreatmentGroup=1. Registry's arm_control=1 therefore does NOT correspond to the paper's control group; SPSS arm 1 is 'Mulligan', an active manual-therapy intervention arm. As configured (arm_include='1,2', arm_control=1), the registry's contrast is Mulligan vs Maitland (both active arms), which does match one of the paper's reported pairwise contrasts and is in fact the study's central stated hypothesis ('Mulligan mobilisation ... will be more effective than the Maitland technique'), but labelling arm 1 as 'control' is incorrect/misleading -- if a true intervention-vs-control contrast is desired, the registry should use arm 3 (e.g. contrasts 1 vs 3 or 2 vs 3) as the control arm. (2) COVARIATES: registry lists covars_published='Age,Gender', but in the paper these are only baseline-balance-check variables (Table 1), not covariates in the primary NPRS model (unadjusted repeated-measures ANOVA); no covariate-adjusted estimate for NPRS is reported. (3) FILE STRUCTURE confirmed: Kiouloukiotis data.sav has 1000 rows, only the first 43 have non-missing TreatmentGroup (rows 44-1000 are empty filler rows), consistent with registry note 'SPSS-Datei mit Fuellzeilen'. Group sizes (Mulligan n=14, Maitland n=14, Control n=15) and NPRS1/NPRS2 means/SDs extracted directly from the .sav file match Table 2 of the paper exactly, confirming outcome_var=NPRS2/baseline_var=NPRS1 are correctly identified.
registry_check.quote_value_labels: Value labels read from Kiouloukiotis data.sav via pyreadstat: TreatmentGroup {1.0: 'Mulligan', 2.0: 'Maitland', 3.0: 'Control'}.

analysis_method_quote: 'Data were analysed using SPSS (Version 29, IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Data entry and verification were performed by two independent researchers to ensure accuracy and minimise errors. Demographic data were summarised using means and Standard Deviations (SDs). The normality of data distribution was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. A Two-Way Repeated Measures Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was conducted to examine between-group differences (Mulligan + Home Exercise versus Maitland + Home Exercise versus Home Exercise only) and within-group changes over time. When a significant group x time interaction was found, post hoc pairwise comparisons between groups at each time point were performed using Tukey's HSD test. The level of statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.' (Materials and Methods, Statistical analysis, p.72)
notes: No single primary outcome is formally declared: the Methods (Outcome measures) state explicitly 'All outcome measures were considered primary and were assessed at baseline and week 2' (p.69), and outcomes studied are pain (NPRS), disability (NDI), cervical ROM (4 measures), pressure pain threshold (2 sites), pain catastrophising (PCS) and kinesiophobia (TSK) -- six distinct outcome constructs, all nominally 'primary'. Per task instructions, the abstract's/methods' first-named outcome (pain intensity / NPRS) was used as the primary outcome for this extraction and primary_outcome_declared set to 'abstract'; NPRS is listed first both in the Abstract ('Pain intensity, functional ability, pain pressure threshold, ROM, pain catastrophising, and kinesiophobia') and in the Methods 'Outcome measures' subsection order (Pain assessment/NPRS is the first subsection). Trial registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06858124); this extraction is based solely on the full-text paper (per task scope) and the registration record itself was not queried online to check its designated primary outcome -- a useful follow-up check. Among the six outcomes, only NDI (disability) showed a statistically significant group x time interaction (F=4.423, p=0.018), but post hoc pairwise comparisons for NDI were not statistically significant for any pair; NPRS (pain), all ROM measures, PPT (both sides) and TSK showed non-significant interactions; PCS interaction was non-significant overall but one specific pairwise post-hoc contrast (Mulligan vs control, p=0.047) was reported as significant despite the non-significant omnibus interaction. Sample size: a priori G*Power calculation for repeated-measures ANOVA (medium effect f=0.25, alpha=0.05, power=0.80) indicated a minimum of 14/group (total n=42); realised n=43 (14/14/15), no dropouts. True control-group (Group 3, TE-alone) NPRS values for reference: baseline 5.07+/-1.87 (n=15), 2nd week 2.80+/-1.32 (n=15) -- these are the values that would represent the paper's actual clinical control arm, as distinct from the registry's current 'control'=Group1(Mulligan) labelling flagged in registry_check.
